title.narrative: Strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities within high climatic and disaster risk areas in Togo.

description.narrative:
The overall objective of this project is to improve preparedness capacities of national institutions and build resilience of local communities to climate change and disaster risks. Specifically, it seeks to: (i) to have a better understanding of disaster risk; (ii) to strengthen governance, preparedness and recovery to better manage disaster risk; and (iii) to make investments in disaster risk reduction for resilience.
To achieve these objectives, the project is structured around three (3) components:
COMPONENT 1: KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF DISASTER RISKS
This component is part of the process of creating an enabling environment for effective operationalisation of the Early Warning System as part of disaster risk reduction in Togo. It is based on the fact that disaster risk management policies and practices should be informed by an understanding of disaster risk in all its dimensions: vulnerability, capacities and exposure of people and property, disaster characteristics and the environment. This knowledge can be used to conduct pre-disaster risk assessments, take preventive and mitigation measures and develop and implement appropriate disaster preparedness and response arrangements. This component targets (2) outcomes:
Outcome 1: Knowledge of disaster risks is increased
The main activities to be carried out include: (i) establishing platforms for knowledge exchange and sharing on DRR and CC; (ii) developing and disseminating guides on EWS best practice; (iii) Developing and disseminating the management tools for the knowledge sharing platform ; (iv) building the capacity of communities in 5 high-risk prefectures on DRR and CC; (v) mapping inhabited flood zones; (vi) acquiring a GIS data analysis and processing tool (Global Mapper) ; (vii) conducting a study on water dynamics in the Oti and Mono river basins ; (viii) conducting a disaster risk study ; (ix) supporting the establishment of a Laboratory of Applied Remote Sensing and Geoinformatics (LTAG) at the University of Lome.
Outcome 2: National stakeholders have a better understanding of disaster risk
Activities under this component include: (i) Developing a mapping of CSOs involved in DRR management and building their capacities ; (ii) designing and disseminating communication materials to raise awareness among communities in 10 prefectures about the various risks in vulnerable areas; (iii) designing, publishing and disseminating posters and comic strips to raise awareness of the various hazards for schools in 5 prefectures in high-risk areas ; (iv) Creating a geohazard disaster portal; (v) establishing a national environmental and climate risk database; (vi) setting up physical and visible risk indicators in vulnerable areas in 7 prefectures.
Component 2: Strengthening governance and disaster risk preparedness
La gouvernance des risques de catastrophe, aux niveaux national, régional et mondial, revêt la plus grande importance pour l’efficacité et l’efficience de la gestion desdits risques. Elle suppose d’avoir une vision claire des plans, des compétences et des orientations, de coordonner l’action de tous les secteurs, et de faire participer toutes les parties prenantes. Lessons from past disasters have revealed that the recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction phase must be prepared upstream and is a major opportunity to 'build back better', including by integrating disaster risk reduction into development policies, thereby building resilience of nations and communities to disasters. There is therefore a need to strengthen disaster risk governance for prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery and rehabilitation. Such strengthening promotes collaboration and partnerships between mechanisms and institutions, with the view to implementing instruments relevant to disaster risk reduction and sustainable development. This second component has two (2) outcomes:
Outcome 3: Policies, strategies, programmes, development projects include the DRR
The activities will focus on : (i) developing community contingency plans in one hundred(100) risk-prone communities in 10 prefectures; (ii) preparation of a guide for integration of DRR into community development plans and local DRR plans; (iii) Updating the national disaster risk reduction strategy and its alignment with the Sendai framework; (iv) Disseminating the National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction ; (v) : Updating the national contingency and ORSEC plans; (vi) Preparing the implementation regulations of the decree establishing the Agency: Regulations for the creation of the National Center for Emergency Operations, regulations for the establishment of an emergency fund ; (vii) development of the national post-disaster recovery strategy; (viii) integration of disaster risk reduction into school curricula in Togo.
Outcome 4: Stakeholders at all levels are equipped for disaster risk management
These include the following activities: (i) building the capacity of the national risk reduction platform stakeholders, including 20% of women; (ii) building the capacity of DRR and CC players on the operationalisation of the "Disaster Risk Measurement, Reporting and Verification" system; (iii) setting up watch committees in high-risk localities, in 5 prefectures including 20% of women ; (iv) building teachers' capacity to integrate DRR into school curricula; (v) installing and energizing regional and prefectoral platforms for disaster risk reduction in exposed areas; (vi) editing the DRR and threats guide for local elected officials ; (vii) training local elected officials in the use of the DRR guide and threats; (viii) establishing and training DRR clubs in schools in high-risk areas ; (ix) establishing and energising leading women's DRR clubs in high-risk areas; (x) carrying out a study to determine the threshold for triggering the ORSEC plan at local, regional and national level; (xi) capacity building of existing forestry officers to address hazards (training and equipment) ; (xii) development of prevention and safety plans (PPMS) in thirty (30) high-risk schools; (xiii) development of preparedness and response plans in one hundred (100) high-risk communities in the Savanes and Maritime regions; (xiv) training of journalists and communicators in the development of communication tools for disaster prevention and management; (xv) training of 20 lifeguards, 20 fire technicians and 10 first aiders; (xvi) strengthening the capacity of the laboratory to measure environmental parameters for post-disaster environmental assessment;
COMPONENT 3: INVESTMENTS IN DISASTER RISK REDUCTION FOR RESILIENCE
Public and private investment in disaster risk prevention and reduction through structural and non-structural measures is critical to building the economic, social, health, and cultural resilience of people, communities, countries, and their property, and to preserving the environment. These elements can contribute to innovation, growth and job creation. Such measures are economically justified and critical to saving lives, preventing and reducing property loss, and ensuring effective recovery and rehabilitation. It aims to achieve the following results:
Outcome 5: Climate information is available in real time and enables the early warning system to be functional
The activities to be implemented include the following: (i) purchasing data collection tools (100 tablets and 100 power banks) ; (ii) purchasing equipment for the upkeep and maintenance of automatic station instruments; (iii) acquiring and installing meteorological instruments and equipment five (5) agrometeorological stations and two hundred (200) complete rainfall stations with support); (iv) setting up the hydrometeorological data processing and archiving system; (v) building the capacity of hydrometeorological monitoring staff in the operation, interpretation, modelling and maintenance of equipment; (vi) upgrading the network of hydrometric stations in the Oti and Mono basins; (vii) setting up a data collection platform via SMS/GSM from smartphones ; (viii) setting up an alarm system based on flood warning thresholds at hydrometric stations in flood risk areas; (ix) strengthening systems and institutional capacities for the transmission and processing of hydrometeorological data in emergency situations; (x) building the capacity of water monitoring staff on the operation, interpretation, modelling and maintenance of equipment; (xi) building a hydrology satellite; (xii) strengthening meteorological services with modern observation and data collection equipment to improve water and weather monitoring system; (xiii) strengthening the hydrological services by installing two (02) automatic stations; (xiv) developing a web and mobile portal for the flood early warning system; (xv) equiping the monitoring room with computer and communication equipment; (xvi) interconnecting the hydrometeorological services to the ANPC watch room (Implementation of a digital platform); (xvii) training the centre's staff in data management and analysis (GIS data, weather forecast and hydro); (xviii) the development of a digital-based operating strategy for the ANPC.
Outcome 6: The resilience of vulnerable communities is built
Activities to be carried out relate to: (i) purchasing rescue equipment (motorized dugout canoes and life jackets) for vulnerable communities; (ii) supporting the cleaning of sanitation facilities in the autonomous district of Greater Lomé; (iii) support for the dredging of basins in 2 high-risk prefectures; (iv) dredging the Azimé-Dossou (Bas Mono) and Wogba (Vogan) silted areas and reforesting 13 hectares of banks ; (v) dredging and rehabilitating the Kpékplémé (Moyen-Mono) retention pond and reforesting 6 hectares of banks; (vi) developing the Vogan lowland and reforesting 14.30 hectares; (vii) developing the Eké watercourse at Atakpamé and reforesting 15.30 hectares of banks; (viii) Developing and reforesting 9 hectares of the banks of the Kpandi and Kpandjo water courses at Sokodé ; (ix) development and reforestation of 12.47 hectares of the banks of the tributaries of the river Kara ; (x) developing and reforesting the Mango lowlands over 8.67 hectares; (xi) building the capacity of a critical mass of local craftsmen per community to assist and advise households in the construction of resilient housing from local materials; (xii) rehabilitating three (3) sites for the reception of disaster victims ; (xiii) Installing and rehabilitating community beacons; (xiv) purchase of life-saving equipment (50 medium-powered motor pumps and their accessories ; 04 hard hull boats; 1000 life jackets; 6 inflatable boats); (xv) organisation of mock exercises in one hundred (100) high-risk communities in the Savanes and Maritime regions.
